subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw expand the core config-file contract to accept YAML files, or keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` canonical and improve the documented programmatic editing path instead?
rationale: This changes core config loading and persistence semantics rather than fixing a broken documented behavior, and repository policy treats config surfaces and fallback behavior as product/compatibility decisions.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Decline YAML for now and document `openclaw config`, `config.patch`, and comment-aware raw-edit guidance as the supported lower-risk path.

options.title: Approve YAML Fallback
options.body: Accept `openclaw.yaml`/`openclaw.yml` only when `openclaw.json` is absent, with explicit parser, precedence, JSON write-back or YAML write-back policy, docs, and tests.

options.title: Split Docs First
options.body: Open a narrower docs task for programmatic config editing and defer the multi-format config decision until there is stronger maintainer demand.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Decline YAML for now and document `openclaw config`, `config.patch`, and comment-aware raw-edit guidance as the supported lower-risk path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current evidence points to recent config contract/docs ownership and product-surface decisions around canonical config behavior.
